subject: Culture
title: Luxury Foods and Status
description: A short lesson to help you apply Luxury Foods and Status.

hook.text: Lobster was prisoner food in colonial America. Now it's a luxury. Price decided its prestige.

buildup.text: Luxury foods signal wealth. Caviar, saffron, truffles—rarity makes them status symbols.

discovery.text: Oysters were cheap street food in 1800s New York. Overharvesting made them scarce, then expensive.

twist.text: In Japan, perfectly shaped fruit sells for hundreds of dollars. Aesthetics outweigh taste.

climax.text: Luxury in food is never about nutrition. It's about what scarcity and story can charge for.

quiz.question: What was lobster's status in colonial America?
options: Food for prisoners and the poor
